summary: Codenames: Pictures swaps the word grid for a grid of surreal, densely-illustrated image cards, making clue-giving looser and more associative than the word version. It plays the same as base Codenames but tends to be friendlier for younger players or non-native speakers since it leans on visual rather than verbal association.
praised: Great for kids, families, or mixed-language groups
Whimsical, imaginative artwork sparks creative clues
Fully compatible/combinable with other Codenames sets
criticised: Images can be more ambiguous than words, leading to messier clues
Some feel it's a bit easier/less sharp than the original
Not a huge structural change if you already own base Codenames

interaction.detail: Like the original, the whole grid of image cards is shared and one player's clue guides their entire team's guesses each turn, with two teams racing on the same board. All game information is public except for the spymasters' hidden knowledge of which cards belong to whom.

scoring.why: Identical structure to base Codenames, just with image cards instead of words; only the order of contacting all agents matters.
scoring.how_you_win: Spymasters give one-word clues pointing to multiple image cards; the first team to have all of its agents correctly identified by teammates wins.
